column5: TRC vol 2 ch 1 says the 1960 state of emergency after Sharpeville (21/03/1960) detained 'over 1 600' people; the course, following Welsh, says 11,503 detained by 08/1960. The two cannot both be right and the TRC figure may be a slip; neither source gives a method, so state the range and mark it [CONTESTED] [check]

TRC vol 2 ch 1: after Sharpeville the ANC and PAC were banned; Pondoland uprising (Ngquza Hill, 06/1960, at least 11 killed; 20 sentenced to death, 11 executed); Sobukwe held nine years; MK formally declared war on 16/12/1961; Poqo set up by the PAC in 09/1961; Church Street bomb 05/1983 killed 19 and injured 217; the UDF (08/1983, over 500 organisations) was banned in 1988 and disbanded 08/1991; state of emergency 06/1986 to mid-1990; Kassinga 1978 killed over 600; the TRC says its own account puts the Soweto uprising as beginning 'on 6 June 1976' (a slip for 16/06/1976)

TRC vol 2 ch 1 framing: it received over 21,000 victim statements and 7,124 amnesty applications; most victims of apartheid-era conflict lived outside South Africa's borders; from 1990 more violations came from people not bound to any political authority, so attributing direct responsibility is hard. It also repeats a claim that CIA information led to Mandela's capture in 1962, which is not corroborated in this text [check]
